findings.title: The `slice-design` docType literal is now scattered across four places instead of one
findings.description: The change introduces `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE = 'slice-design'` as a canonical constant, but the same literal is still hardcoded in the pre-existing frontmatter registry: `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:76` (`values: ['slice-design']`), `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:148` (`slice: 'slice-design'`), and `packages/core/src/schema/frontmatterSchema.ts:185` (`docType === 'slice-design'`). AGENTS.md is explicit: "Never scatter comparison values across code. If a value is used in conditionals, switch cases, or lookups, define it once … Changing a value should require editing exactly one place." As written, renaming the docType requires editing four files, and the new constant is dead weight because nothing else consumes it. Either have `frontmatterSchema.ts` import `SLICE_DESIGN_DOC_TYPE` (or move the constant into a shared, browser-safe module both can import without a cycle), or drop the new constant and reuse the registry's existing spelling — but do not leave both spellings live.

findings.title: Project resolution and the "Project not found" message are duplicated across two command files
findings.description: `resolveTemplatePath` in `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:34-46` repeats the project-resolution preamble that already exists in `packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts:160-172`: constructing a `FileProjectStore`, calling `resolveProjectWorktree({ project: opts.project }, store)`, calling `store.getById(id)`, and throwing the byte-identical user-facing string `Project not found: '${id}'. Run cf project list to see available projects.` The only real difference between the two is the final step (one checks `project.projectPath`, the other checks the resolved checkout root). AGENTS.md requires "Do not duplicate logic. Respect DRY" and defines shared values once. Extracting a single helper into `packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts` — e.g. `resolveProjectCheckout(opts)` returning `{ project, checkoutRoot }` and owning the not-found error — would remove the duplicated message and keep the two `validate` subcommands from drifting as resolution rules evolve.

findings.title: The `--json` error path is never actually exercised by the new CLI test
findings.description: The `for (const json of [false, true])` loop at lines 205-214 exercises the `--json` flag but only asserts an empty stdout and exit code 2. The structured JSON error contract on stderr is never checked, because JSON mode is enabled by `setJsonMode()` in `packages/cli/src/index.ts:178` — and this test builds its own `Command` and calls `registerValidateCommand` directly, bypassing `index.ts`. `isJsonMode()` therefore returns false, and `handleError` takes the plain `console.error` branch rather than the JSON branch in `packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts:41-52`. Production behavior is correct (the real entry point enables JSON mode), so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect: the `--json` variants of the three exit-2 cases silently test the non-JSON error path twice. Setting `process.env.CF_JSON = '1'` for the JSON iterations and asserting the stderr payload parses as `{ error: true, message: … }` would close it.

findings.title: The core API accepts an empty file list and returns an empty result set
findings.description: `validateSliceDesignFiles(templatePath, files)` runs `preflight` over `files` and returns `[]` when the list is empty — no `SliceDesignValidationError` is raised, even though the class docstring at lines 34-40 says "Usage and template problems throw `SliceDesignValidationError`" and the file header says "every file argument is checked before any result is produced". The empty-list usage guard therefore lives only in the CLI at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:62-66`. That is fine for the one caller today, but the function is exported from `@context-forge/core/node` and the slice design explicitly anticipates reuse ("A later `cf check` rule can reuse them"), where a caller passing an empty list would get a silent "nothing to validate" instead of the usage error. Moving the empty-list check into `validateSliceDesignFiles` would make the core contract match its own documentation.

findings.title: Each validated document is read from disk twice
findings.description: `validateFile` calls `parseFrontmatter(file)` — which itself does a full `readFile` in `packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:29` — and then reads the same file again at lines 100-105 to extract its headings. For a batch of N designs this is 2N full reads where N would do. The impact is small for typical batches and the fix (a text-overload on `parseFrontmatter`) touches a shared parser, so this is informational; worth revisiting only if `cf validate design` is ever pointed at large document sets.

findings.title: Faithful port of the guide script with a clean pure/file-layer split
findings.description: I compared the port against the original `project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/validate-slice-design` line by line. The heading normalization (`packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignValidator.ts:32-41`), the "heading followed by the trimmed `<!-- required -->` marker" rule (lines 44-55), the fenced-code skip (lines 58-73), the prefix match that lets `# Slice Design: {slice-name}` match a concrete title (lines 76-83), and the PASS/FAIL + `  missing: <heading>` output contract in `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:49-59` all match the bash original, including its intentional divergences (real markdown heading syntax only, CRLF stripping, quoted `docType` accepted via `parseFrontmatter`). The deliberate leniency widenings are documented in the slice design rather than left implicit. The exit-code contract (0 pass / 1 fail / 2 usage-or-template) is implemented consistently, including the deliberate `[files...]` optional-argument trick at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:92-93` so that "no files" exits 2 instead of Commander's 1. The tests use the real template and real slice designs rather than synthetic fixtures, which is the right way to catch a template-format change.
